body:
Global crypto markets took a significant hit on November 6, absorbing a brutal combination of macro shock and sentiment collapse. Total market capitalization fell to $2.58T, down -6.61% over the last 24 hours, with $106.8B in volume suggesting this was not a low-liquidity drift but a genuine flush. The Fear & Greed index cratered from 50 (Neutral) yesterday to 28 (Fear) today, one of the sharpest single-day sentiment reversals in recent weeks. Per CoinDesk, over $1 billion in bullish bets were liquidated while ETF flows provided no offsetting support in the spot market, meaning the long side got hit from both directions simultaneously. BTC dominance held at 59.1% with ETH dominance at 10.6%, a ratio that tells you capital is not rotating into alts — it is simply leaving.

Bitcoin printed $75,720 at time of writing, down -4.17% on the day and -2.03% on the week, with hourly momentum effectively flat at -0.23% — the selloff has largely occurred, not ongoing. Volume of $44.58B is elevated and consistent with a forced liquidation event rather than orderly distribution. The trigger, per multiple CoinDesk reports, was the October U.S. jobs print: 165,000 non-farm payrolls against a consensus estimate of 65,000, a staggering beat that immediately reset rate-cut expectations and hammered risk assets. Bitcoin has stabilized in the near term but traders should watch the $75,720 area closely — a failure to reclaim any ground from here risks confirming this as a new lower range rather than a dip. The recovery to watch is a push back above the round $80,000 level; absent that, the technical picture deteriorates meaningfully on a weekly basis.

ETH led the major losers with a -5.67% drop to $2,235.01, underperforming BTC by a significant margin and carrying $17.62B in volume. The relative weakness in ETH is notable given its 7-day figure is technically +0.11%, meaning this session erased a week of quiet outperformance in a single day. XRP was the session's worst performer at -8.03%, landing at $1.19 with $2.76B in volume and a -4.88% 7-day slide — the most sustained selling pressure among tracked majors. SOL dropped -3.57% to $90.92 and is down -6.70% over 7 days, with the asset carrying additional idiosyncratic headwinds after reports that Solana's Shanghai event was halted over unauthorized promotion. The relative bright spots, if they can be called that, were DOT at +0.62% on the day, AVAX at -2.26% with a positive 7-day figure of +1.47%, and UNI at +0.79% on the week despite a -1.90% session. BNB at $696.29 was the most resilient major, down only -1.33% on the day, though this tells you more about positioning than any fundamental divergence.

The macro context is doing the heavy lifting here. A jobs print of 165,000 against a 65,000 estimate is not a beat — it is a repudiation of the entire dovish rate narrative that had been supporting speculative assets through October. Rate-cut bets get repriced aggressively on a print like this, and crypto, which had been trading with a loose correlation to Fed sensitivity, bore the consequences immediately. On the regulatory front, the picture is mixed but not clean: Nigeria set new crypto licensing rules and banned algorithmic stablecoins, Thailand moved to block Bitget as its local acquisition faces uncertainty, and per Cointelegraph, Democrats' midterm sweep raises questions about the trajectory of the CLARITY Act. Ethereum's development timeline also faces friction, with devs signaling they will not fork Glamsterdam on Hoodi until smart contract risks are resolved — incremental negative for ETH's near-term narrative.

The immediate catalyst to watch is any Fed communication that walks back or contextualizes the jobs number, since that is the proximate cause of today's reset. A single data point does not necessarily change the trajectory, but until officials speak, markets will price the hawkish interpretation. On the upside, a resumption of ETF inflows would be the clearest signal that institutional demand is using this dip as an entry point rather than stepping back entirely — today's data showing no ETF support during the selloff is the most bearish single data point in the brief. Watch XRP specifically: an -8.03% single-day move on top of a -4.88% weekly loss suggests either forced selling or a specific catalyst not yet fully surfaced. BTC holding $75,720 into the weekend is the minimum bull case; breaking below risks triggering the next leg of technical selling with no obvious support structure visible in the near-term data. The sentiment reset from 50 to 28 in one session is a warning that positioning was far more crowded than the surface suggested.
